channel.title: AvoKind Journal
channel.description: Whole-food nutrition, ingredients and evidence explained clearly.

item.title: What are the benefits of avocado?
item.description: What are the benefits of avocado? A science-grounded guide to avocado fiber, unsaturated fat, nutrients, carotenoid absorption, and what human studies actually show.

item.title: What is nopal? Nutrition, fiber, and what the research says
item.description: What is nopal? Learn what cactus pads are, what nopal fiber does, and what human studies do—and do not—show about digestion and post-meal glucose.

item.title: Does freeze-drying preserve nutrients?
item.description: Does freeze-drying preserve nutrients? Learn how lyophilization works, what it tends to preserve well, what can still be lost, and how it compares with heat drying.

item.title: What is dietary fiber, and why does it matter?
item.description: What is dietary fiber? Learn how fiber supports digestion, cholesterol and glucose control, how much the FDA Daily Value is, and why different fibers behave differently.

item.title: Are smoothies healthy? What changes when you blend whole foods
item.description: Are smoothies healthy? Learn what blending changes, what happens to fiber and glucose response, how smoothies differ from juice, and how to build a balanced smoothie.

item.title: What are the benefits of spinach?
item.description: What are the benefits of spinach? A grounded guide to folate, vitamin K, carotenoids, potassium, dietary nitrate, and what human studies actually show.

item.title: Does ginger have health benefits? What human studies actually show
item.description: What are the benefits of ginger? Learn where human evidence is strongest, why most studies use supplements, and what that means for culinary ginger in food.

item.title: What are the benefits of turmeric? Curcumin evidence and its limits
item.description: What are the benefits of turmeric? Learn what curcumin studies show, why bioavailability matters, and why supplement research cannot be applied directly to culinary turmeric.

item.title: Why do some vitamins need fat? Fat-soluble vitamins and carotenoid absorption
item.description: Why do some vitamins need fat? Learn how vitamins A, D, E and K and carotenoids are absorbed, and why eating vegetables with some dietary fat can matter.

item.title: Added sugar vs. natural sugar: what is the difference?
item.description: Added sugar vs natural sugar: learn what the FDA label means, why total sugar and added sugar are different, and why the food matrix still matters.
